noah: RFC follow-up: need a compact default for EU-resident write handling when primary is down. block vs escrow vs proxy? pick one and owners.

anya: short: default = fail-closed. we can add opt-in paths but default must be legally safe.

priya: runtime note: escrow (async accept on standby) exists as a prototype. main issues: idempotency, cache finality, and vector replication gating.

ops: ops concern: escrow backlog risk. add circuit-breaker: if escrow_queue_age_p95 > 300s or size>10k, auto-disable escrow feature.

legal-bot: policy: EU-resident data can't be processed outside EU without explicit tenant consent (auditable token). any fallback requires consent token check.

sre-oncall: pragmatic hybrid: default=fail-closed; enterprise tenants may opt in to execute-escrow with consent token; non-sensitive dev tenants may opt in to proxy-sync. owners: runtime=sre, api=devx, legal=legal-bot, ops=ops.

priya: idempotency: require idempotency_key on all opt-in flows. escrow records store request_id and payload_hash; replayer dedupes on request_id.

noah: cache rule: responses from escrowed executions get header X-Redwood-Finality: pending and must not be used for long-term replication. clients can request only-final.

ops: metrics to add: residency_block_rate, escrow_accept_rate, escrow_queue_age_ms, consent_check_latency_ms. alert if consent_check_latency_ms>500ms.

legal-bot: consent token format suggestion: CONSENT::{tenant_id}::{consent_id}::{ts_iso}::{scopes}. introspect endpoint required. retain audit logs 7y.

priya: billing: charge at standby execution time. mark reconciliation metadata so we don't double-bill. product to update pricing docs.

noah: decision line: Default = fail-closed; enterprise opt-in = execute-escrow with consent token + idempotency_key; developer opt-in = proxy-sync for non-PII. Owners as above.

sam.k: timeline: RFC follow-up PR by Wed, small runtime spike next week to validate escrow latencies. closing when PR merged.

noah: thanks — closing thread when PR lands. :white_check_mark:
